security_spec.violation_condition: RTL CSR module still references ERR_CFG field as 'msi_en' (bit 3) after spec rename to 'msi_sel', while simultaneously implementing HWCFG2.msi_en (bit 26) as a new capability indicator. If the Chisel/Verilog CSR decoder uses name-based field resolution (e.g., auto-generated from spec JSON), the old wire name 'msi_en' now ambiguously maps to HWCFG2 bit 26 instead of ERR_CFG bit 3, causing the MSI wired-or-MSISelect signal to read from the wrong register — or causing ERR_MSIADDR/ERR_MSIADDRH availability gating to check ERR_CFG.msi_sel (configuration) instead of HWCFG2.msi_en (capability), exposing MSI address registers when hardware does not support MSI.
security_spec.summary: Field rename ERR_CFG.msi_en→msi_sel collides with new HWCFG2.msi_en capability bit; stale RTL signal names referencing 'msi_en' cause MSI interrupt path selection and address-register availability gating to read wrong CSR source, enabling MSI hardware interfaces when unsupported or routing interrupts to incorrect destination

findings.finding: RegHwcfg2 bundle is the obsolete v0.8 layout containing only prio_entry[15:0] and rrid_transl[31:16]. The spec (riscv-iopmp/extensions/registers.adoc lines 91-108) defines HWCFG2 as a 32-bit register with 10 fields: prio_entry[15:0], prio_ent_prog[16], non_prio_en[17], rsv[25:18], msi_en[26], peis[27], pees[28], sps_en[29], stall_en[30], mfr_en[31]. The RTL has NONE of the upper 16 bits. Bit 26 (msi_en) falls within the rrid_transl field, which is initialized to 0 (IopmpParams.rrid_transl=0 at line 52) with a disabled write path (lines 817-819 commented out). Software reading HWCFG2 at offset 0x0010 always sees bit 26 = 0, incorrectly concluding MSI is unsupported. This is the root function_loss in the security spec: MSI address registers appear absent to software, so MSI interrupt configuration is skipped entirely.

spec_citations.excerpt: HWCFG2 register fields: prio_entry[15:0], prio_ent_prog[16], non_prio_en[17], rsv[25:18], msi_en[26] (R, Indicates whether the IOPMP supports MSI extension), peis[27], pees[28], sps_en[29], stall_en[30], mfr_en[31]
The bit msi_en in register HWCFG2 indicates whether the IOPMP supports MSI extension.

findings.finding: RegHwcfg2.apply() initializes only prio_entry and rrid_transl. Neither msi_en nor the other 7 extension capability bits (prio_ent_prog, non_prio_en, peis, pees, sps_en, stall_en, mfr_en) are initialized. Note that these capability indicators are already tracked separately in HWCFG0 (IopmpParams.peis=1 at line 42, IopmpParams.pees=0 at line 43, IopmpParams.stall_en=0 at line 41, IopmpParams.mfr_en=0 at line 44) and in the RegHwcfg0.toUInt encoding (line 516), but they need to be replicated in HWCFG2 per the new spec layout. A new parameter (e.g., hwcfg2_msi_en = 1 since the ERR_CFG.msi_sel storage and msidata field exist in hardware) must be added alongside the other capability parameters.

spec_citations.excerpt: HWCFG2 all fields with their Default column showing IMP (implementation-defined) for capability bits

findings.finding: ERR_CFG bit 3 field is named 'msi_en' instead of the spec-mandated 'msi_sel'. The spec (registers.adoc line 175) defines bit 3 as 'msi_sel' with semantics: '0x0: wired interrupt, 0x1: MSI'. The PR title explicitly states 'rename ERR_CFG.msi_en to ERR_CFG.msi_sel'. The old name 'msi_en' now collides with HWCFG2.msi_en (bit 26, read-only capability indicator). The comment on this field correctly describes MSI/wired selection behavior, confirming this is a naming error, not a semantic mismatch. A name-based CSR decoder or auto-generated header would resolve 'msi_en' to HWCFG2 bit 26 (capability) instead of ERR_CFG bit 3 (selection control).

spec_citations.excerpt: msi_sel[3:3] WARL: Indicates whether the IOPMP triggers interrupt by MSI or wired interrupt: 0x0: wired interrupt, 0x1: MSI
The bit msi_sel in register ERR_CFG indicates whether the IOPMP triggers interrupt by MSI or wired interrupt.

findings.finding: IopmpParams.msi_en (default=0) holds the ERR_CFG bit 3 default for MSI/wired selection. This parameter name collides with the new HWCFG2.msi_en (read-only capability indicator at bit 26). After the rename to ERR_CFG.msi_sel, this parameter should be renamed to 'msi_sel' and a separate new parameter 'hwcfg2_msi_en' (default=1) should be added to indicate the MSI extension capability is present in hardware (the RTL instantiates msidata storage at line 628, writable at line 831, and has RegErrmsiaddr/RegErrmsiaddrh class definitions at lines 724-729).
findings.snippet: val msi_en             = 0    // [WARL] Indicates whether the IOPMP triggers interrupt by MSI or wired interrupt

spec_citations.excerpt: msi_en[26:26] R, IMP default: Indicates whether the IOPMP supports MSI extension.

findings.finding: ERR_CFG.msi_en (to be renamed msi_sel) write path at line 829 has no gating on HWCFG2.msi_en. Per the reference model (iopmp_reg.c lines 708-710), writes to ERR_CFG.msi_sel and ERR_CFG.msidata must be conditionally gated: 'if (iopmp->reg_file.hwcfg2.msi_en) { iopmp->reg_file.err_cfg.msi_sel = err_cfg_temp.msi_sel; iopmp->reg_file.err_cfg.msidata = err_cfg_temp.msidata; }'. When HWCFG2.msi_en=0 (MSI extension not present), writes to msi_sel and msidata should be ignored/hardwired to 0. Currently there is no such gating — software can write msi_sel=1 even when HWCFG2.msi_en reads 0, creating a configuration inconsistency and a potential privilege_escape: if downstream hardware or future versions DO gate on HWCFG2.msi_en, the current unconditional write path silently permits MSI configuration that should be impossible.

Ctrl interrupt generation always asserts io.int (wired interrupt pin) when ERR_INFO.v=1 and ERR_CFG.ie=1, completely ignoring the msi_sel configuration bit. There is no FSM state to issue an MSI write to ERR_MSIADDR with msidata when msi_sel=1. Per the reference model (iopmp_interrupt.c lines 35-81), the correct behavior is: (a) if HWCFG2.msi_en=0, always use wired interrupt; (b) if HWCFG2.msi_en=1 and ERR_CFG.msi_sel=0, use wired interrupt; (c) if HWCFG2.msi_en=1 and ERR_CFG.msi_sel=1, issue an MSI memory write to the address formed from ERR_MSIADDR/ERR_MSIADDRH with data from ERR_CFG.msidata, and set ERR_INFO.msi_werr on bus error. The current behavior is a correctness gap: the wired interrupt pin is always used regardless of configuration, making the msi_sel configuration bit effectively non-functional.

spec_citations.excerpt: generate_interrupt: when HWCFG2.msi_en=0, only wired interrupt; when msi_en=1 and msi_sel=0, wired; when msi_en=1 and msi_sel=1, generate MSI write to ERR_MSIADDR with msidata; on bus error, set ERR_INFO.msi_werr=1
The address is MSI address and is specified by ERR_MSIADDR and ERR_MSIADDRH, while the content to write is stored in the field msidata in the register ERR_CFG.

findings.finding: ERR_MSIADDR (offset 0x0078) and ERR_MSIADDRH (offset 0x007C) are not implemented. The register offset constants exist (lines 94-95), and Bundle class definitions exist but are commented out as 'not implemented' (lines 724-730). No instances exist in RegMap (lines 766-776), no read entries in the MuxLookup (lines 855-867), and no write logic. Per the spec (msi.adoc lines 8-10), ERR_MSIADDR and ERR_MSIADDRH hold the MSI target address and are the registers the IOPMP writes to when generating an MSI. The availability of ERR_MSIADDRH is gated by HWCFG0.addrh_en=1 AND HWCFG2.msi_en=1 (msi.adoc line 10). Even if HWCFG2.msi_en were correctly implemented as 1, software would be unable to configure the MSI target address, making MSI delivery impossible.

val reg_errmsiaddr_addr_offset      = 0x0078.U(16.W) // errmsiaddr
val reg_errmsiaddrh_addr_offset     = 0x007C.U(16.W) // errmsiaddrh

spec_citations.excerpt: ERR_MSIADDR[31:0] WARL: The address to trigger MSI. Available only if HWCFG2.msi_en=1. ERR_MSIADDRH[31:0] WARL: The higher 32 bits. Available only if HWCFG0.addrh_en=1 and HWCFG2.msi_en=1.
The address is MSI address and is specified by ERR_MSIADDR and ERR_MSIADDRH.

findings.finding: specver is hardcoded to 8 (line 28). The PR adding HWCFG2.msi_en capability bit and renaming ERR_CFG.msi_en to ERR_CFG.msi_sel is part of a spec revision that changes the register layout (HWCFG2 goes from 2-field v0.8 layout to 10-field extension layout). specver must be bumped so software can detect which register layout the hardware implements. Without this, software cannot distinguish an old IOPMP (where HWCFG2 had only prio_entry and rrid_transl) from the new one (where HWCFG2 has msi_en at bit 26).

The HWCFG2 read path at line 860 returns reg_hwcfg2.toUInt = Cat(rrid_transl, prio_entry), which lacks msi_en at bit 26 and all other extension capability bits. A CSR read from offset 0x0010 always returns bits [31:16]=rrid_transl (all 0s, since init=0 and write path disabled) and [15:0]=prio_entry. Bit 26 (msi_en) is therefore always 0. Software reading HWCFG2 concludes MSI extension is absent and skips MSI interrupt configuration. This is the concrete manifestation of function_loss. Additionally, no read entries exist for ERR_MSIADDR (0x0078) or ERR_MSIADDRH (0x007C) — these offsets fall through to the default (0), further confirming the MSI address registers are inaccessible.

spec_citations.excerpt: HWCFG2 read must return msi_en at bit 26 per the register layout

findings.finding: RegMapIO exposes o_reg_errcfg_msi_en (line 753) with the old name. After the rename to msi_sel, this should be renamed to o_reg_errcfg_msi_sel. Additionally, no output exists for o_reg_hwcfg2_msi_en (the capability bit) which downstream consumers like the Ctrl module would need to gate MSI behavior. The signal o_reg_errcfg_msi_en wires to reg_errcfg.msi_en (line 878) but is never consumed by Ctrl (Ctrl only references o_reg_errcfg_ie for interrupt enable and o_reg_errinfo_v for error valid status).

val o_reg_errcfg_rs = Output(UInt(1.W)) // bus response suppression
val o_reg_errcfg_msi_en = Output(UInt(1.W)) // MSI enable
val o_reg_errcfg_msidata = Output(UInt(11.W)) // MSI data

findings.finding: HWCFG0.addrh_en comment documents the OLD gating rule: 'ERR_MSIADDRH (if ERR_CFG.msi_en = 1) are available'. In the new spec (msi.adoc line 10), ERR_MSIADDRH availability is gated by HWCFG2.msi_en (capability), NOT ERR_CFG.msi_sel (runtime selection): 'ERR_MSIADDRH is available only when HWCFG0.addrh_en = 1 and HWCFG2.msi_en = 1'. The actual hardware is benign (addrh_en is hardwired to 1 at line 47, read-only), but the documented dependency references the wrong register. This matters if addrh_en were ever made conditional or if the comment is relied on by verification.
findings.snippet: val addrh_en = UInt(1.W) // [R] Indicate if ENTRY_ADDRH(i) and ERR_MSIADDRH (if ERR_CFG.msi_en = 1) are available

spec_citations.excerpt: ERR_MSIADDRH is available only when HWCFG0.addrh_en = 1 and HWCFG2.msi_en = 1.
